extracted.intended_audience: Participants and potential participants of MER Forum workshops (mathematicians, mathematical scientists, mathematics educators, and K-12 teachers)
extracted.subtask_description: A mailed survey instrument (multiple versions for different audiences) used to collect participants' demographics, prior and current mathematics/teacher-preparation activities, involvement in math-education reform, perceptions of MER publications and events, workshop impacts on practice, and intentions for future activities and networking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of mathematics teacher preparation activities (past two years)
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of mathematics teacher preparation activities (e.g., pre-service or in-service math content or methods courses, curriculum development, outreach workshops) have you been involved with during the last two years at your university/college? Please provide as many specific examples as possible and group into the following categories: K-12 education (indicate grade level(s)), Undergraduate level (includes pre-service education, designing undergraduate curricula), Graduate level, Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific examples for each category; specificity is emphasized and extra pages may be attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other mathematics activities involvement (past two years)
rubrics_metrics.description: What other types (other than teacher preparation) of mathematics activities have you been involved with during the last two years at your university/college? Please provide as many specific examples as possible and group into the following categories: K-12 education (indicate grade level(s)), Undergraduate level, Graduate level, Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific examples for each category; extra pages may be attached if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop relevance: enhancement of current activities
rubrics_metrics.description: How do you think the information presented at this MER workshop will enhance the mathematics education reform activities you are currently involved with? Describe how specific workshop information will interact with your current educational activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific examples showing the connection between workshop content and current work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics participants wished were addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you think of any mathematics education reform topics that you would have liked had been addressed at this workshop but were not? Please describe the types of topics you would have liked addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended; request types of topics and specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenters' pedagogy modeled
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you feel that the presenters, in general, modeled good pedagogy? Please describe what you considered examples of good and/or poor pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of observed pedagogical practices, both positive and negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned immediate changes to teacher preparation (next month)
rubrics_metrics.description: What might you do differently as a result of the workshop in your teacher preparation activities during the next month? (Please provide specific examples.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should list concrete actions they plan to take in the short term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned short-term changes to teacher preparation (next semester)
rubrics_metrics.description: What might you do differently as a result of the workshop in your teacher preparation activities during the next semester? (Provide specific examples.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide course- or program-level changes expected within the next semester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned longer-term changes to teacher preparation (next year)
rubrics_metrics.description: What might you do differently as a result of the workshop in your teacher preparation activities during the next year? (Provide specific examples.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe anticipated policy, curricular, or pedagogical changes over the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities to continue because of the workshop (next month)
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of activities might you continue with as a result of the workshop in your teacher preparation program during the next month? (i.e., what you learned reinforced what you had been doing; please provide specific examples.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List activities that will be continued or reinforced in the immediate term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities to continue because of the workshop (next semester)
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of activities might you continue with as a result of the workshop in your teacher preparation program during the next semester? Please provide specific examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sustained actions or programs for the upcoming semester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities to continue because of the workshop (next year)
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of activities might you continue with as a result of the workshop in your teacher preparation program during the next year? Please provide specific examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe longer-term sustained activities or initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spreading the word in department
rubrics_metrics.description: What might you do in terms of 'spreading the word' at your mathematics department about math education reform upon your return (e.g., offering seminars, talking to colleagues, reporting to administrators)? Please be specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete dissemination strategies and target audiences within the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with education faculty and cross-departmental connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your department (or you specifically) have a working relationship with the education faculty at your institution? If yes, please describe briefly the extent of this relationship. If you are a mathematics educator in an education department, please describe your relationship with the mathematics department. Also: have you received any information from this workshop that might help you make connections with the education (or mathematics) department upon your return? Please explain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe existing collaborations and how workshop information could facilitate connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of physical presence at workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: What beneficial aspects of the workshop could only be obtained by being physically present at the Baton Rouge gathering? That is, which aspects of the workshop would not have been as beneficial via some other mode of communication (written materials, telephone contact, video-tapes, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify interactive, networking, or experiential elements requiring in-person attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects not requiring physical presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you feel that there were any aspects of the workshop that you need not have been physically present to have benefited (e.g., you could have received the same understanding via written material, video, or some other medium)? Please explain why or why not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify content or materials that could be delivered remotely and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of MER and newsletter usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about how participants found out about MER, whether they have attended MER banquets or special sessions, and which sections of the MER newsletter they find helpful (e.g., information on basic MER activities; feature articles regarding programs/projects; essays on state/future of mathematics education; other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents circle applicable newsletter sections and indicate awareness/attendance of MER events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and use of CBMS Issues in Mathematics Education volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you aware of the MER publications in the CBMS Issues in Mathematics Education volumes? Have you read any of these CBMS publications? To what extent are the CBMS volumes useful to you? If useful, please explain how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale responses (not at all / a little / considerably / extremely) and open-ended explanation if rated useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of MER special sessions on meeting/workshop attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent did the existence of the MER special sessions at the Joint Mathematics Meetings influence your decision to attend the Meetings? To what extent did these MER special sessions influence your decision to attend a MER workshop? To what extent were these special sessions useful to you?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond on a four-point scale (not at all / a little / considerably / extremely) and explain usefulness if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: MER workshop attendance history (which workshops attended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you attended a MER workshop? If yes, which of the listed MER workshops have you attended (multiple options listed by date/location)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circle all that apply; used to gather longitudinal attendance data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for attending MER workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Why did you attend this/these MER workshop(s)? (Check all that apply.) Options include: colleague recommended, department chair recommended, invited speaker, invited small group presenter, wanted to meet people who share interests in math education reform, wanted to meet people who share research interests, personal expenses paid, wanted to visit city/university, wanted to meet MER co-directors, wanted to exchange ideas with peers, interested in theme, other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple selections allowed; captures motivations for attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographics: gender, race/ethnicity, year of birth
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard demographic items: gender, racial/ethnic classification, and year of birth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents circle categories or fill in year; used for descriptive analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest educational degree
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the highest educational degree you hold? (Options provided including Ph.D. in math, Ph.D. in another field, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the single option that applies; 'other' allows specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership in professional organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: To which of the following mathematics, mathematics education, and education professional organizations do you belong? (List includes AMS, MAA, SIAM, AWM, NCTM, AMATYC, AERA, Other.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circle all organizations to which you belong; provide names/acronyms for 'other'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic rank and years of faculty service
rubrics_metrics.description: If you work in an academic institution, what is your present rank? How many years have you been a faculty member at the school where you presently work (including this year)? How many years have you been a faculty member at other schools?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select rank and report total years; used to contextualize respondent experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness/attitudes about MER's impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement-scale items: e.g., 'I am more aware of the issues in math education reform as a result of the MER Forum'; 'MER duplicates services provided by other organizations'; 'After participating in one MER workshop, I felt comfortable calling/contacting MER colleagues I had just met about professional matters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a four-point agree/disagree scale (Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree); if respondents select agree, they may be asked for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reported change in teaching because of MER
rubrics_metrics.description: I have changed my own teaching because I have been involved with MER. If yes, follow-up: I attribute the impetus for these changes to (a) information in MER newsletters/publications/networking with colleagues, and/or (b) information and experiences at MER workshops. Please provide two examples of changes in your classroom teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent indicates change, they provide up to two concrete examples and indicate attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of contacting MER colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Since your first MER workshop, how frequently have you contacted MER colleagues about: (a) personal teaching issues? (b) mathematics education reform issues? (c) mathematical research issues? (Options: never, once, 2-5 times, 6-10 times, more than 10 times.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark frequency for each contact topic area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to attend another MER workshop under expense conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Would you attend another MER Forum workshop if the topic were of interest to you and: (a) all expenses were paid? (b) you had to pay for your own transportation and conference fee? (c) you had to pay for all of your own expenses, including room and board?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to each expense scenario separately to gauge sensitivity to cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most vital reforms needed in mathematics education (open-ended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe the two most vital reforms needed in mathematics education, in your opinion (e.g., types of curriculum, pedagogy, or assessment improvements you feel are most important).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended; respondents may attach additional pages if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived benefits/drawbacks to hosting a workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: If you work at an academic institution, have you hosted a workshop at your institution? What do you perceive as the benefits of and drawbacks to hosting a workshop? If you have already hosted, comment on how easy or difficult it was to work with MER in this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe logistical, institutional, and professional pros/cons and experiences hosting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of involvement in specified mathematics education reform activities (past two years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a four-point scale (not at all / a little / considerably / very), indicate the extent you have been involved with the following reform activities during the past two years: a) K-12 curriculum reform; b) Undergraduate curriculum reform; c) Increasing participation of underrepresented minorities (not including women); d) Increasing participation of women; e) Undergraduate programs for math majors; f) Reform related to graduate mathematics education; g) Undergraduate remedial courses; h) Calculus reform; i) Undergraduate programs for pre-service teachers; j) Programs for in-service teachers; k) Involvement with specific groups of K-12 students (e.g., gifted & talented or special needs students); l) Reform efforts at the school district level; m) Reform efforts from statewide initiatives; n) Other (please specify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents circle a number for each listed activity; captures breadth and intensity of involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of primary reform involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe the type of mathematics education reform with which you are most involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended; respondents may attach additional pages for extended descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimates of departmental faculty involvement by activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Please estimate the number of faculty in your department involved in the following activities: K-12 math education reform; Undergraduate math education reform (for both math and non-math majors); Undergraduate teacher preparation reform; Graduate math education reform for math grad students; Graduate math education reform for math education grad students; Teacher enhancement for in-service teachers; Research mathematics. Also: what is the total number of faculty in your department?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric estimates for each activity and total department size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of collaboration with education department faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: How often do you formally or informally collaborate with educators in education departments on your own campus? (Scale: never, once per year, once or twice per semester, once or twice per month, more than twice per month.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the response that best matches typical collaboration frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of work time among professional activities (hours/week)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using provided definitions, divide your work time among these professional activities: Teaching; Mathematics Research and Scholarship; Mathematics Education Reform Activities; Service; Administration; Other. Indicate number of hours/week you spend on each activity during a typical week and the number of hours you believe your department prefers for promotion/tenure/merit raise decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both actual weekly hours and perceived departmental preference for evaluation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitudinal items about departmental value/support for reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Please indicate agreement (four-point scale Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree) with statements such as: (a) Involvement in mathematics education reform is highly valued in my department; (b) In my department, the atmosphere toward mathematics education reform is one of acceptance and support; (c) During the past five years, the atmosphere in my department toward mathematics education reform has changed, becoming more positive (if agree, give two specific examples); (d) During the past five years, new projects/programs related to mathematics education have been supported by my department (if agree, provide two examples); (e) I usually consult literature in the field of educational research for information about mathematics education reform; (f) I usually consult mathematics educators (professionals in education) for research about mathematics education reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use four-point agreement scale; items c/d request examples if respondent indicates agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to be contacted for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: May we have your name, phone number and email address so that we may contact you if we have any questions or would like any further information about the MER Forum?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contact details if willing to be contacted; return questionnaire in stamped envelope.
